prompt: CMT-03 has a budget of 1250000, has spent and committed 940000, and forecasts 1400000. What sets that forecast?
options: The larger of its budget and actual plus commitment, raised by a contingency the engine adds to every line still in progress.
The positive forecast its engineer entered, which the rule takes ahead of both the budget and the spend.
Its 640000 spent projected to completion at its progress of 55.0000 percent, which the rule switches to once a line is past half done.
Its actual plus commitment of 940000, carried up by the overrun the line has already booked against its budget of 1250000.
explanation: Left to the fallback, CMT-03 would forecast its budget of 1250000; the entered 1400000 wins, so its variance of -150000 exists only because someone typed it.

prompt: CMT-03's entered forecast is replaced by 900000, below the 940000 already spent and committed on the line. What does the line forecast?
options: 940000, because the engine floors an entered forecast at the money already spent and committed before it accepts the figure.
1250000, because a forecast below the spend to date is not credible and the rule falls back to the larger of its two formula figures.
Nothing, because a forecast below actual plus commitment is refused with an input error that names the cost item carrying it.
900000, because any positive entered forecast is taken as typed.
explanation: The rule never compares a positive entry with the spend (finding EC5-1); an entry of 1 on the same line forecasts 1.

prompt: CMP-05's completion work is cancelled and its forecast field is set to 0. What does the OFON-1 report show?
options: No saving: the line still forecasts 5600000, the EAC stays 27600000 and the variance stays -550000.
A saving of 5600000, because a zero forecast takes the line out of the EAC while its budget stays in the authorised total.
An EAC that drops to take in only the 1200000 committed on the line, since a cancelled line still owes the orders already placed.
A refusal naming CMP-05, since a forecast of 0 fails the input check in the same way that a negative progress figure does.
explanation: 0 is not positive, so the rule falls back to the larger of the 5600000 budget and the 1200000 spent and committed; a descope saves nothing until the budget itself is changed.

prompt: DRL-01 has spent 9800000 and committed 2600000 on a budget of 14200000 and is 72.0000 percent complete, with no entered forecast. Why does it forecast 14200000?
options: The rule projects the 9800000 spent from 72.0000 percent complete, capped at budget.
A line forecasts its budget until its progress reaches 100.0000 percent.
The rule takes the larger of the budget and the 12400000 spent and committed, and the budget is larger.
The engine divides the budget by the AFE's CPI of 1.009377 and rounds the result back up to the budget, as the line is ahead.
explanation: The fallback reads money spent and promised and nothing else; it never reads progress or CPI, so DRL-01's 72.0000 percent plays no part in its forecast.

prompt: DRL-01, LOG-04 and CMP-05 each show a line variance of 0. What does that 0 establish?
options: Only that spend plus commitment has not yet passed the budget and nobody has entered a forecast.
That the three lines are on budget, since each will finish at its authorisation.
That the lines will save money, since the fallback rounds an underrun down to 0.
That the three lines have not started, since only progress books a variance.
explanation: 0 is the rule's floor: without an entered forecast a line's forecast is at least its budget. DRL-01 is 72.0000 percent complete and still shows 0.

prompt: With CMT-03's other figures unchanged, an entered forecast of 1 makes it forecast 1, and an entered forecast of 0 makes it forecast 1250000. What separates them?
options: The engine reads 1 as a forecast stated in millions and scales it up before comparing, while it reads 0 as a field left blank.
Only the sign test: 1 is positive and taken as typed, while 0 is not positive and falls back to the formula.
A forecast of 1 is held for review and shown as entered, while a forecast of 0 is taken as a descope and the line keeps its budget.
A floor at actual plus commitment applies only to a zero entry and leaves 1 alone.
explanation: Nothing checks a positive entry against the 940000 already spent and committed, so 1 stands; 0 falls to the larger of 1250000 and 940000.

prompt: OFON-1's variance at completion is -550000. How is it built?
options: Budget less actuals less commitments, the money the AFE has left to spend.
The overrun on CSG-02 alone, with the AFE's CPI of 1.009377 applied to the rest of the budget to project the lines not yet done.
Actuals of 15090000 set against planned value on the report date, since a variance compares money spent with the calendar.
Budget 27050000 less EAC 27600000, which is -400000 on CSG-02, -150000 on CMT-03 and 0 on the other lines.
explanation: Variance is budget less EAC, so an overrun is negative; the line variances add to the same -550000.

prompt: "suite test: entered forecast" has nothing spent or committed and forecasts 140.0000 on a budget of 100. What makes its overrun different from the 130.0000 in "suite test: committed past the budget"?
options: It is no overrun, since a variance is booked only once actuals are recorded.
The engine leaves an entry with no spend out of the EAC until money is spent.
Nothing, since both lines forecast the larger of budget and actual plus commitment.
It rests on a typed judgment with nothing spent, while 130.0000 is money already spent and promised.
explanation: The first returns variance -40.0000 on an entry of 140 alone; the second has 70 spent and 60 committed, which pass the budget of 100 and give -30.0000.

prompt: The published line "negative entered forecast is ignored (the S-curve ignores it too)" has a budget of 100, 20 spent and an entered forecast of -50. Why does it forecast 100.0000?
options: The engine refuses the -50 with a message naming the line and restores the budget, as it does for a negative progress figure.
The -50 is booked as a saving, and the variance is then clamped at 0.0000.
-50 is not positive, so the rule compares the budget of 100 with the 20 spent and takes the larger.
The engine reads the minus sign as a typing slip and uses 50, then floors the forecast of that line at its budget of 100.
explanation: Ignored is not refused: nothing on the screen says the -50 was never used, and the line returns EAC 100.0000 and variance 0.0000.

prompt: CMP-05 forecasts 5600000. Can a reviewer tell from that whether its forecast field is blank, 0 or negative?
options: No, since none of the three is positive and each falls back to the same 5600000 without a word.
Yes, since a negative forecast is refused with a message and a blank is not.
Yes, since a zero forecast drops the line from the EAC and a blank does not.
Yes, since the rule used column prints entered for any figure typed into the forecast field, whatever the sign of that figure.
explanation: "Not yet estimated", "cancel this work" and a typing slip produce one forecast: the larger of 5600000 and the 1200000 spent and committed.

prompt: Had CSG-02's budget of 3900000 been copied into its forecast field, as editing a line did before EC5-0, what would the line report?
options: 4300000 and -400000, since entries are floored at the money spent.
A refusal, since an entry below the actual of 4300000 is rejected.
A forecast of 3900000 and a variance of 0, hiding the 400000 overrun already spent.
4300000 and -400000, since a forecast equal to its budget is ignored.
explanation: A copied budget is a positive entered forecast and wins; the repaired Suite no longer copies it, but a figure copied by hand does the same damage.

prompt: Before EC5-0 the Cost Breakdown table showed the budget as the forecast and the PDF and Excel variance was budget less actual. What does the repaired Suite show on OFON-1?
options: 27050000 as the table's forecast, since it shows what was authorised.
27600000 and -550000 on the tiles, the table, both exports and the Top 5, all from the one rule.
The one rule on screen, while the PDF and Excel exports keep budget less actual so that earlier issued reports still reconcile.
27600000 on the tiles and table, while the Top 5 keeps its own old rule.
explanation: After the Suite repair the tiles, Cost Breakdown table, PDF, Excel and Top 5 read one rule, so a disagreement between two reports points at the data or the export date.

prompt: Every repaired screen now reads the one forecast rule. What has that fixed, and what has it left alone?
options: It fixed the forecast, which now extrapolates from progress and CPI.
Nothing, since every old screen already showed 27600000.
It made the rule stricter, refusing a forecast below the spend.
It makes the screens agree, and every screen still shares the rule's limits.
explanation: No screen forecasts a line under its budget without an entered forecast, and none reads progress, CPI or a non-positive entry, so OFON-1's EAC is still 27600000.

prompt: A partner reads OFON-1's EAC of 27600000 as a projection from performance to date. What is it?
options: The budget of 27050000 scaled up by the ratio of actuals to earned value across the lines, which is how cost performance is projected.
14200000 + 4300000 + 1400000 + 2100000 + 5600000: three budgets, one spend and one entered figure, added.
The actuals of 15090000 plus the remaining budget divided by CPI, the standard projection of cost to completion from performance.
The 15090000 spent plus the 5000000 committed plus the budgets of unstarted lines.
explanation: The rule reads budgets, actual plus commitment and entered forecasts and never progress, so the EAC carries no reading of performance.

prompt: A line is half done and already past its budget on spend and commitment, with no entered forecast. What does the rule forecast for the half still to do?
options: Nothing, since it forecasts only what is spent and committed until someone enters a forecast.
The rest of the budget at the line's progress rate, since the rule extrapolates a line from its progress once spend passes the budget.
Twice its spend and commitment, projected from its half-done progress.
The whole budget again, as a line past its budget gets a fresh one.
explanation: The rule refuses to forecast what has not been committed; CSG-02 forecasts 4300000 because its spend passes its budget and nothing more is committed, and a half-done line past its budget would stop at its spend and commitment just the same, whatever its progress.
